# Declaring shape checks over tabular data

The bundled `verifier-shape-checks` executor runs in-process and is reachable by
name with no service wiring. Both the rows and the checks arrive as node
attributes.

## The template

```yaml
name: shape-checks-demo
version: "1"
nodes:
  - type: verifier
    executor: verifier-shape-checks
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          checks:
            type: array
            default:
              - kind: pk_unique
                severity: error
                config: {field: id}
              - kind: numeric_range
                severity: error
                config: {field: value, min: 0, max: 100}
              - kind: row_count_absolute
                severity: error
                config: {min: 1}
          rows:
            type: array
            default:
              - {id: a, value: 10}
              - {id: b, value: 20}
              - {id: c, value: 30}
```

## Rows that satisfy every check

```bash
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/nodes/$IID/verifier"
```

The node settles fresh, and the verifier's own output records how many checks it
ran and how many rows it read — `verifier_checks: 3`, `verifier_rows: 3`.

An author enforces data shape without writing or deploying a verifier.

## Rows that violate a check

```yaml
          rows:
            type: array
            default:
              - {id: a, value: 10}
              - {id: a, value: 20}
              - {id: c, value: 250}
```

The node has no fresh run and one failed run, and the terminal signal names the
failing check kind: `terminal/error/verifier/check_failed/pk_unique`.

## The declaration is what governs

Re-submit the clean rows under a stricter declaration — the same three checks
plus a `no_nulls` check on a field the rows do not have:

```yaml
              - kind: no_nulls
                severity: error
                config: {field: note}
```

Rows accepted under one declaration are rejected under the stricter one, with
`terminal/error/verifier/check_failed/no_nulls`. An author tightens or loosens
enforcement by editing the declaration and nothing else.

## An unimplemented check kind fails loudly

```yaml
          checks:
            type: array
            default:
              - kind: no_such_check
                config: {}
```

The node fails with `verifier/attribute_invalid` rather than passing silently.
An author who mistypes or invents a check kind learns it from the run instead of
believing their data was checked when it was not.

That mistake is caught when the node runs, not at template registration.
